dimension_assessments.summary: The window specifies the client boundary, local and remote placement posture, marker-before-.git root fallback, selection intent, and diagnostics storage/presentation boundary.
Client ownership, catalog support, primary and supplementary attachment modes, and diagnostics-only capability limits are explicit.
ServerSpec inputs and the per-server diagnostic storage key and presentation consumers are identified, although detailed algorithms are gaps assessed separately.
Several boundaries are explicit, but catalog payload, deterministic root and selection rules, diagnostics semantics, and security contracts are not executable from the window.
Lifecycle state is named but no lifecycle vocabulary, transition graph, capability projection, diagnostic lifecycle, or invalidation transition contract is supplied.
Puppet Master is explicitly the LSP client and lifecycle owner; OpenCode is explicitly only reference input, and remote LSP authority cannot be a hidden local mirror.
Plans/LSPSupport.md owns the LSP-specific client and protocol constraints while referenced owner documents retain their SSOT boundaries.
Settings > LSP, status surfaces, Problems, editor markers, and Assistant or Interview context are named consumers.
The GUI must expose effective overlapping-server state and must not show unavailable or degraded attachments as healthy; diagnostic presentation surfaces are identified.

Unhealthy-state fabrication is prohibited, but lifecycle failure states, retries, restart and reconnect behavior, root loss, selection failure, diagnostic cleanup, and provisioning recovery are absent.
Automatic downloads, custom executable configuration, environment fields, and diagnostics-to-LLM data flows lack normative trust, secret-handling, consent, redaction, routing, and retention controls.
The window does not define how root, registry, server, capability, or diagnostic changes invalidate sessions and propagate to GUI and assistant consumers.
Lifecycle supervision and cross-boundary observability lack retry, restart, logging, metric, trace, correlation, and operator-control contracts.
A truncation token is preserved, but all capacities, performance targets, scheduling, cancellation, and overload behavior are unspecified.
OpenCode reference compatibility and underscore storage spelling are stated, but legacy-value migration, unknown-value handling, downgrade behavior, and receipts are absent.
The listed criteria and validators establish plan provenance and indexing rather than observable product behavior or failure handling.
Consequential choices remain open for catalog membership, root and server selection, lifecycle and recovery, diagnostics merging, trust and privacy, capacities, migration, and propagation.

The authoritative core leaves unresolved the full catalog matrix, deterministic precedence and tie-breaking, state vocabularies, diagnostic lifecycle, quantitative limits, and security or privacy policy.
